subject: Spatial Count models for only unmarked individuals in secr?

messages.author: be58eaa5a0f65d19
messages.subject: Spatial Count models for only unmarked individuals in secr?
parts:
Hi All,

I am a bit new here but have learned a lot recently about mark-resight models in secr, which relies on having repeat sightings of known individuals, but can incorporate counts of unmarked individuals. Recently, I have been asked to estimate density of an entirely unmarked population using spatial count models (which I am unfamiliar with). So I am wondering:

1. Can SMR models be fit using just information on counts of unmarked individuals?
2. If not, does the secr package have any functions to fit spatial count models (or something analogous)?

Thanks for any information people can provide,

Andrew

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Spatial Count models for only unmarked individuals in secr?
parts:
1. Yes, sort of. I'm thinking of Chandler & Royle (2013) Annals of Applied Statistics 7: 936–954 DOI: 10.1214/12-AOAS610 and Ramsey et al. (2015) Journal of Wildlife Management 79:491–499; DOI: 10.1002/jwmg.851, and more recent papers that I haven't followed (I would guess it's in the Kery & Royle AHM book). Precision can be very poor without further assumptions or data.
2. No, this is beyond 'secr'.
Murray
